Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: replacement transparent square pixel-art character portrait for the historical investigation game Memórias Licantropicas, Rio de Janeiro 1890.
Input images: Image 1 (bentinho.png) is PRIMARY STYLE AND FRAMING REFERENCE; Image 2 (escobar.png) is supporting STYLE reference. Image 3 (bras_cubas.png) is the OLD EDIT TARGET for character identity ONLY, whose excessively realistic painting style must be completely redrawn.
Primary request: redraw Brás Cubas so he looks convincingly made by the SAME pixel artist as Bentinho and Escobar. Use their stylized slightly oversized head, large readable expressive eyes, simplified facial anatomy, dark stepped outlines, coarse crisp visible square pixel clusters and restrained warm earth-tone shading. This is a complete stylistic redraw, not a sharpened/downsampled realistic painting.
Subject invariants: pale Brazilian aristocratic man in late middle age, swept-back gray hair, clearly blue eyes, short uneven white/gray stubble beard, dark charcoal nineteenth-century frock coat, simple dark waistcoat, high ivory collar and ivory cravat. Proud, reserved, subtly sardonic expression, neutral and alive as in a file portrait. Preserve his distinctive older identity, but translate it into the stylized reference cast. Simpler clothing without ornate brocade.
Composition/framing: ONE head-and-shoulders bust, square 1:1 canvas, three-quarter view looking slightly RIGHT like Bentinho and Escobar, entire hair silhouette and both shoulder outlines fully INSIDE the canvas. Match reference proportions and transparent margins: about 7% above hair, 6% on both sides, and 4% below rounded bust edge; centered and visually balanced. No cropped hair or shoulders.
Style: charming expressive handcrafted 16-bit game pixel art. Match Bentinho and Escobar closely in face simplification, eye size, pixel coarseness and overall visual weight. Use broad grouped pixels for hair, stubble and clothing, no individual realistic hairs, pores, intricate textiles or glossy cinematic shading. Readable at 96x96 logical pixels.
Background: genuinely transparent alpha, including around and below the bust. Keep full-color source; the game applies newspaper grayscale separately.
Constraints: no scenery, frame, border, text, watermark, props, blood, death marks, supernatural cues or effects. No photorealism or realistic digital-painting anatomy. Do not copy either reference character's identity; only their visual language.

Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: production sprite animation sheet, transparent pixel-art detective game set in Rio de Janeiro1890.
Input image: player.png is the SAME detective Floriano, both identity and exact pixel-art style reference. Preserve face, dark hair, small dark mustache, warm medium-brown skin, chestnut-brown jacket with pocket notebook, charcoal waistcoat with brass buttons, ivory collar, dark trousers, brown boots, adult body proportions.
Primary request: completely redraw the WALKING POSES into a convincing alternating two-leg walk cycle, fixing the reference where the same front leg keeps kicking forward. Exact TEN full-body poses, laid out in EXACTLY FIVE columns and TWO rows, with generous transparent gutters and padding; every figure looks to the RIGHT in the same side-on three-quarter angle. This is ONE character repeated in animation phases, not ten different men.
Layout in reading order:
Top row cell1: relaxed standing idle both feet on ground.
Top row cell2: same standing idle, tiny breathing difference only.
Top row cell3 WALK1: near leg leads forward and heel contacts ground, far leg stretched backward toe on ground; far arm leads forward.
Top row cell4 WALK2: near foot flat supports weight, far heel lifts as far leg begins swinging forward underneath pelvis; knees slightly flexed.
Top row cell5 WALK3: near leg straight under body bearing weight, far knee bent and moving forward PAST the support leg, far foot lifted; both legs almost cross underneath torso.
Bottom row cell1 WALK4: near leg behind, far thigh swings forward with knee slightly bent and foot preparing contact; near heel lifts.
Bottom row cell2 WALK5: OPPOSITE contact to WALK1: far leg leads forward with heel contact, near leg stretched backward with toe contact; near arm leads forward.
Bottom row cell3 WALK6: far foot flat supports weight, near heel lifts as near leg swings under pelvis.
Bottom row cell4 WALK7: far leg straight below body bearing weight, near knee bent passing forward, near boot lifted.
Bottom row cell5 WALK8: far leg behind, near thigh swinging forward, preparing return to WALK1.
Critical animation invariants: ALTERNATE which leg is in front across the cycle; clearly distinct foot positions; arms swing in opposition to legs. Normal relaxed walking, NOT jogging, hopping, marching or kicking. Stable head and torso scale, jacket length, hair and face across every cell. Consistent foot baseline in EACH row, no cropped feet/hair/arms, no overlapping cells. Near trouser leg slightly lighter charcoal and far trouser leg darker, consistently, to make leg alternation readable. Subtle vertical head movement only, no dramatic pose changes. Full body and broad transparent margins.
Style: exact same handcrafted expressive 16-bit raster pixel art as source, clean dark stepped outlines and visible square pixel clusters, warm restrained earthy colors. No blurry painting, photorealism, vector, outlines of grid, cell numbers, labels or text. TRUE TRANSPARENT alpha background; no floor, shadow rectangle, scenery, watermark, props added. Preserve notebook in jacket pocket. Output one landscape sheet aspect about 1.7:1, 5 columns x2rows, ten poses total.
